# TRIPWIRE INDEX (DEC-12: every documented invariant has one)

**This file is a machine-read contract, not a status note.**
`test/unit/ci_workflow_tripwire.test.ts` asserts that the `TRIPWIRES` array in
`scripts/verify.ts` equals the first column of the table below, EXACTLY (the
12-vs-14 drift found 2026-07-09 stays fixed), and that every listed file exists
on disk. `scripts/ci/hermetic.sh` runs a SUBSET of the same list — the hosted
tier may run fewer gates, never unknown ones.

Adding a tripwire means adding a row here AND to `scripts/verify.ts` in the same
change; either alone is a red gate.

Home-of-record rule (amends S2-45): the tripwire index lives HERE, in
`engineering/`, because it is mechanically enforced and must travel with the
code. Coverage STATE — measured baselines, per-subsystem progress, the
known-open gap list — stays in `rewrite/LEDGER.md`, which links here and never
duplicates this table.

| test/unit/install_ip_gate_tripwire.test.ts | The pre-auth install window's address allowlist is FAIL-CLOSED (2026-08-24, audit P2-6, `engineering/wire_contract/WC-2026-08-24-install-ip-gate-fail-closed.md`). Behind `installIpAllowed` sits an UNAUTHENTICATED installer that rewrites `../private/.env` and spawns psql; until this change an unset `DEDALO_INSTALL_ALLOWED_IPS` admitted EVERY address — the wrong default on exactly the deployments where the browser wizard is the reasonable path (a container stack, a VM, a hosted box). Unset, empty or separator-only now means LOOPBACK ONLY (`DEFAULT_INSTALL_ALLOW_ENTRIES`), an entry is `loopback` / a literal address / a CIDR block / `any`, and `any` is the ONE spelling that opens it and appears in no default. Asserts the default against nine non-loopback addresses (the IPv4-mapped spelling and the docker bridge gateway included) and every loopback spelling, that no other wildcard-looking token (`*`, `all`, `ANY`, `0/0`) opens anything while `0.0.0.0/0` opens only its own family, and the whole of `ipInCidr`: v4/v6 in and out of range on and off a byte boundary, no cross-family match, and nineteen malformed pairs that deny WITHOUT THROWING (an exception inside a pre-auth predicate is itself the vulnerability). ALSO A PROSE SCAN, because a fail-closed default decays in two directions and only one of them is code: six documents plus the generated config artifacts stated "unset = open", and a reader who believes that either goes looking for a lock already on or "restores consistency" by reopening the code. Rule A bans the old wording across `docs/install/**`, `docs/development/ts_install_internals.md`, `docs/config/config.md`, `engineering/PRODUCTION.md`, `install/sample.env`, the catalog source and `docker-compose.yml`, with the four verbatim removed sentences as a positive control so a pattern that matches nothing fails; rule B demands every file naming the key STATE the new default, with an anti-vacuity floor; and the compose file must ship the `DEDALO_INSTALL_ALLOWED_IPS` passthrough, since docs alone do not fix a shipped artifact. One narrow exemption, decided per match on the surrounding window and proven narrow by its own test: `DEDALO_ERROR_REPORT_ALLOWED_IPS` is deliberately open when unset (that receiver is off unless switched on, invisible when off, throttled and token-checked). Honest limits: it proves the PREDICATE and the PROSE, not that dispatch calls it (`install_gate.test.ts` drives the 403), and it cannot see past `clientIp` — a request with no `X-Forwarded-For` resolves to the sentinel `'local'` in `server.ts::clientIpFromRequest`, so a bare TCP listener with no proxy still reads a remote peer as loopback |
| test/unit/proxy_trust_tripwire.test.ts | A HEADER IS ONLY AS TRUSTWORTHY AS ITS TRANSPORT (P2-4, 2026-08-24). `X-Forwarded-For` is a request header — anything that can open a connection writes it — so `clientIpFromRequest` reads it only on a listener an operator declared to be behind the reverse proxy (`TRUSTED_PROXY_TRANSPORT`, default `socket`), and on any other transport uses the CONNECTION's peer address (`server.requestIP`). The hop arithmetic was already right (`TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` from the right, never the left-most entry) and ran on EVERY listener, including the direct TCP port a browser reaches with no web server in front — where the client simply chose the value: a fresh login-throttle bucket per request (the brute-force evasion the arithmetic exists to stop), attacker-chosen addresses recorded as fact in dd544 activity rows, and — since the install gate matches the literal `127.0.0.1` — a forgeable claim to be loopback, which is why the function's old "never an authorization input" comment was false. A second bug in the same expression: `Math.max(0, len - hops)` clamped a SHORT header to index 0 and returned its LEFT-MOST entry, i.e. the attacker's own value, whenever fewer entries arrived than the operator declared hops; a short header is now treated as forged (peer address, else the `proxy-malformed` sentinel, which cannot satisfy a loopback check and cannot amplify into an install-wide lockout because `buildThrottleKey` carries the username). Asserts both directions (forged single value, forged chain, forged loopback, no-peer fallback), that `createRequestContext` defaults to UNTRUSTED so no future caller inherits the spoofable path by omission, that the hop count is read PER CALL rather than captured at import (a module-level const makes any such gate assert only its own default), the throttle consequence (same peer + different forged headers = ONE bucket), and that exactly one production call site exists and it passes a context. Mutation-verified in both directions. Honest limit: it proves the resolution rule, not that Bun reports the peer correctly, nor that a declared transport matches the deployment — `TRUSTED_PROXY_TRANSPORT=tcp` on a port with no proxy is trusting the caller again, which is why the default is `socket` |
| test/unit/password_cost_tripwire.test.ts | Password cost has ONE definition, and stored hashes CATCH UP to it (P2-7, 2026-08-24). Every `Bun.password.hash` call passed `{ algorithm: 'argon2id' }` and inherited whatever the runtime chose, so the cost of a heritage institution's credentials was a property of whichever Bun version was installed the day each account was created — changing silently under a runtime upgrade in EITHER direction, with nothing in the repo recording what was used. Worse, there was no path back: `isArgon2Hash` passes any `$argon2…` string through untouched by design (it is what makes export→import round-trips and the v6 migration work), so a hash made under weak parameters stayed weak forever, since no login, password change or migration ever revisited it. Now `src/core/security/argon2_params.ts` states m=65536,t=3 once and all six hashing sites import it — including the AUTHZ-03 DECOY, which must stay cost-matched because `Bun.password.verify` costs what the STORED hash declares, so a cheaper or dearer decoy makes the failure path distinguishable again by exactly the difference. The gate asserts no call site passes its own options (matched to the STATEMENT end, since the decoy hashes `crypto.randomUUID()` and a lazy match would truncate at its paren and report a compliant site), that `memoryCost`/`timeCost`/`parallelism` appear as CODE nowhere else (comments stripped — `parallelism` is an ordinary English word in the external transport's prose), a census floor so an emptied scan cannot pass silently, and the UPGRADE-ONLY rehash predicate in both directions: the runtime's old t=2 default and a weaker memory axis upgrade, the target is left alone, and a STRONGER hash is never rewritten downwards (PHP's `password_hash(PASSWORD_ARGON2ID)` used m=65536,t=4 — a routine login rewriting those would be a silent regression, and they are exactly the hashes an install carries from before the rewrite), with an unparseable hash left alone because not knowing a credential's cost is not a reason to rewrite it. Mutation-verified both ways. KNOWN BOUNDED WINDOW, recorded rather than papered over: raising t=2→t=3 means an account that has not logged in since the upgrade verifies ~25 ms below the decoy — a weak residual enumeration signal, far under the ~70 ms-vs-0 ms gap AUTHZ-03 closed, bounded by the same throttle, and self-closing per account at its next login. Honest limit: it proves the parameters are stated once and the predicate is right, not that the work is actually done (the runtime's business) nor that the rehash lands — `rehashStoredPassword` is deliberately best-effort and off the login's critical path |

FOUR ASSERTIONS: (1) no entrypoint outside `TOKEN_OWNERS` DECLARES a name `vars_tokens.less` declares — matched on declaration (`--x:` in a rule), never on `var(--x)` USE, since consuming the palette is the whole point of it, and only on the INTERSECTION with the palette's own name set, so a tool's OWN token (`--tool_indexation`) stays legal; (2) the entrypoints that actually emit a palette token EQUAL `TOKEN_OWNERS` — set equality, not ⊆, so an owner that stops emitting fails as a stale entry instead of leaving the app unstyled behind a green run, and each entry carries a reason string naming the DOCUMENT it renders into and why main.css is not there (length-gated, so it cannot decay to `''`); today the sole owner is `main.less`, the SPA document stylesheet; (3) the converse (1) and (2) cannot see — the entrypoints NOT injected into the main.css document (named WITH their document, since no CSS reveals where its bytes land: the two PDF.js iframe sheets) must declare every `var(--…)` they use, or they render with every value blank. The palette's NAMES are read from the LESS SOURCE (228 literal declarations, no interpolation, and it is a partial — compiling it would mean a bespoke second `less.render`, the copy of the build the sibling gate refuses to keep), while the consumers are read COMPILED via `buildOne`: the duplication arrives TRANSITIVELY several imports deep, so a scan of a tool's own `.less` would see nothing and a scan of its committed `.css` would go green on a stale artifact. A self-test asserts the palette source still declares >200 names (228 since the `--ut_*` fold-in below) — a moved `vars_tokens.less` would make every intersection trivially empty. (4) every partial in `EMIT_FREE_PARTIALS` compiles to ZERO bytes — the assertion an adversarial pass proved (1)-(3) could not make, since all three are keyed to names `vars_tokens.less` ALREADY declares, so adding a token to `vars.less` (the file 39 stylesheets import, called "vars", that every doc pointed at for three years) re-emitted it from 36 entrypoints with the gate fully green. The list is a record of path → reason, each reason carrying the MULTIPLIER (importers, of which entrypoints); adding the next widely-imported partial is one line in it, not a new test. Also from that pass: the root-selector match covers `body`/`*`/`html body`, not just `:root`/`html`, because a `body { --color_white: red }` reaches every rendered element exactly as `:root` does and the narrower regex passed it. THERE IS NO SECOND PALETTE ANY MORE: `theme_tokens.less` used to have the shape `vars.less` had — LESS `@font_*`/`@size_*` vars plus an emitting `:root` — and its 28 `--ut_*` tokens (light + dark) shipped in BOTH `main.css` and `unit_test.css`, which land in the same runner document (`test/client/index.html` links them together). Closed on 2026-08-02 by DELETING the special case rather than splitting a second pair: the light block moved into `vars_tokens.less`, the dark one into `theme_dark.less`, and `theme_tokens.less` kept only the LESS vars — so its importers changed no line, it joined `EMIT_FREE_PARTIALS` (2 importers, both entrypoints), `OWNED` went 200 → 228 names, and a re-declared `--ut_*` is now caught by assertion (1) like any other palette token instead of by a pinned two-entrypoint allowance. `theme_token_parity.test.ts` gates the light/dark pairing of the 28. (5) only the files NAMED in `PALETTE_FILES` may declare a palette token on a GLOBAL ROOT (`:root`/`html`/`body`/`*`, with any attribute qualifier). Assertions (1)-(2) work in ENTRYPOINT space, where the answer is always `main.less` — so a NEW partial anywhere in its ~120-import graph can declare `:root { --color_white: red }` and retune the app document-wide with the whole suite green; an adversarial pass landed exactly that payload and everything passed. This one asks which FILE wrote the declaration, which only SOURCE space can answer (by the time a partial reaches `main.css` it is flattened in with no record of its origin), so it walks LESS braces keeping a selector stack and resolving `&` — deliberately over-approximating, since a false positive is a conversation and a false negative is the hole. The allowlist is the three real axes — `vars_tokens.less` (light), `theme_dark.less` (theme), `redesign/_tokens.less` (design, an ORTHOGONAL axis, which is why the rule is "the named palette files" and not "two files") — each stamped with the axis it varies, and set-checked so a stale entry that no longer declares anything fails too. A SCOPED override stays legal and needs no entry: that is the sanctioned custom-property idiom, bounded by its selector. This gate exists because "there is no third file that can grow a fourth palette" was the STATED REASON the `--ut_*` palette was folded in rather than split into its own pair, and an unenforced justification is how the next maintainer learns the rule was never real. Honest limit: it proves nobody re-DECLARES the palette, not that the values are right or that a document actually receives it — the two PDF.js sheets' self-sufficiency is asserted, but the claim that they are the only standalone documents is hand-maintained. |

| test/unit/crap_complexity_ratchet.test.ts | src/core/ CYCLOMATIC COMPLEXITY may only SHRINK (2026-08-09) — a per-file shrink-only ratchet over `engineering/crap_complexity_baseline.json`, which holds the measured census (this row deliberately restates no number, per S2-45: the artifact is the state, this is the rule). WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A THRESHOLD: CRAP(m) = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + comp collapses to CRAP = comp at full coverage, so "CRAP <= 6" IS a hard cyclomatic cap of 6 — and about a fifth of this tree's functions exceed it by construction, so a flat cap could never pass and was REJECTED. The gate FREEZES the measured debt and forbids growth instead of demanding it be paid at once. TWO HALVES: (a) SHRINK-ONLY — no file may exceed its frozen max, the frozen count of over-cap FUNCTIONS and FILES may not move (the census counts functions, which is what catches a new over-cap function hiding under an already-listed file's max), and a file now BELOW its entry, an entry at/under the cap, or an entry for a deleted/moved file is RED, because a stale entry silently loosens the ratchet (19 -> 5 unfrozen may climb back to 19 unseen); (b) NEW-FILE CAP — a file absent from the baseline may not exceed complexity 6: frozen debt is a legacy fact, new debt is a choice, and the only two answers are simplify it or add a NAMED exemption whose reason and staleness are themselves asserted (the exemption map is EMPTY). (c) THE COVERAGE-EXEMPT LIST (2026-08-11, `engineering/crap_coverage_exempt.json`) — the third part, and the only one about COVERAGE rather than complexity: which `src/core/` functions no gate may EXECUTE, and WHY. Two admissible reasons only — UNRUNNABLE (it destroys or mutates what no scratch surface contains: the shared schema, the media tree, the machine, a third party, or the run-shared cache/session/scheduler singletons of Bun's single test process) or VACUOUS (a zero-decision projection/delegation whose only available assertion restates the code or re-reads the same host). Per DEC-12 the reason must live NEXT TO THE CODE, so the load-bearing assertion is the MARKER check — an ATTACHMENT check, not a whole-file substring test (GATE-42b: an entry named a file that only IMPORTED its symbol after an extraction, and its marker had been left above a DIFFERENT function; both `includes` checks passed). Every entry's symbol must be DECLARED in the named file (a top-level function/const/let/class — an import or a call is reported as 'extracted or renamed, point the entry at the declaring file'), and the marker must be ATTACHED to that symbol in one of three shapes: in the contiguous comment run immediately above the declaration; inside the declaration's own span (an arm exemption), which ends where the NEXT declaration's doc block begins; or in a REASONED block comment (slash-star, at least `NAMING_BLOCK_MIN_LINES` = 4 lines) that NAMES the symbol — one header covering several passes of a file, the reason written out. A bare `// COVERAGE-EXEMPT: see X below` line or a one-line block is a cross-reference, not an attachment; a marker elsewhere in the file is an orphan and is red. Positive controls: an import-only symbol, an orphaned marker on the neighbour, the arm shape, the naming shape, a marked second declaration whose block must not count for the unmarked first, the bare cross-reference line and the thin block (both refused). The JSON is the INDEX over those markers, never a substitute. AST-only and hermetic: no DB, no network, no coverage run, so it joins the hermetic CI tier.
